Rashi on Chullin 83a:10:1.hebrew: למה לי למיתני את האם לחתן - ליתני במוכר זו לחתן וזו לכלה, ומאי פסקה דנקט לחתן אם ולכלה בת:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:10:1.english: Why do I [need] to teach “the mother to the groom” - Let [the Mishnah] teach “where one sells this one to the groom and that one to the bride,” and what is the fixed rule [i.e., why does it specify] that it stated the mother for the groom and the daughter for the bride:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:10:2.english: For the groom's household to exert effort - and to prepare a feast more than the bride['s household]:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:12:1.hebrew: שזיכה לו ע"י אחר - המוכר הזה מסר את השור לאדם אחר שלא בפני הלוקח, ואמר לו: זכי בשור זה לפלוני, להיות לו בדינר בשר:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:12:1.english: [Where] he transferred ownership to him through another - This seller handed the ox over to another person in the buyer's absence and said to him: "Acquire this ox on behalf of So-and-so, for him to have a dinar's worth of meat."

Rashi on Chullin 83a:12:2.hebrew: דזכות הוא לו - מסירה זו זכות היא לו, דהא לא סגי ליה בלא בשר:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:12:2.english: Where it is a benefit to him - This transfer [of ownership] is a benefit to him, since he cannot do without meat:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:12:3.hebrew: חוב הוא לו - להוציא הוצאות, הפסד הוא לו:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:12:3.english: It is a disadvantage to him - To incur expenses is a loss for him:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:12:4.hebrew: אין חבין לו - דאין אדם נעשה שליח לחבירו שלא מדעתו להפסידו, אבל להרויחו אנן סהדי דניחא ליה, לפיכך זכין ואין חבין:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:12:4.english: One cannot act to his disadvantage - For a person cannot become an agent for his fellow without his knowledge to cause him a loss, whereas to profit him, we are witnesses [i.e., we can presume] that he is amenable [to it]; therefore, one may act to [another's] benefit, but one may not act to [his] disadvantage:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:13:1.english: On Torah law - that his money acquires [it] for him without pulling:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:14:1.hebrew: דבר תורה מעות קונות - מכיון שנתן מעות למוכר, אין אחד מהם יכול לחזור, דגמרינן מהקדש, דכתיב: "ונתן הכסף וקם לו":
Rashi on Chullin 83a:14:1.english: By Torah law, money effects acquisition - Once [the buyer] has given money to the seller, neither one of them can retract, for we derive [this] from consecrated property, as it is written: "And he shall give the money, and it shall become his":

Rashi on Chullin 83a:14:2.hebrew: ומה טעם אמרו משיכה קונה כו' - דאי מוקמת להו לפירי באחריות הלוקח משנתן מעות, אי מתרמי דליקה בבית המוכר שהפירות שם, לא טרח לאצולינהו; אבל סתם מושך, ממטי להו לביתיה:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:14:2.english: And what is the reason they said pulling effects acquisition, etc. - For if you place the produce in the buyer's responsibility from [the time] he gives the money, if a fire happens [to break out] in the seller's house where the produce is [located], he will not bother to save it; whereas ordinarily, one who pulls [the produce] brings it to his [own] house:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:15:1.hebrew: היום הולך אחר הלילה - שחט האם משחשכה, לא ישחוט הבת כל הלילה וכל היום המחרת; אבל שחט האם ביום, שוחט הבת בלילה, דאין הלילה הולך אחר יום:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:15:1.english: The day follows the night - [If] one slaughtered the mother after dark, he may not slaughter the daughter all that night and all the following day; however, [if] he slaughtered the mother during the day, he may slaughter the daughter at night, because the night does not follow [the] day:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:15:2.hebrew: את זו דרש - משום דבעניינא דקדשים כתיב אותו ואת בנו, איצטריך למדרשה, כדתניא בגמרא:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:15:2.english: [Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma] expounded this - Because [the prohibition of] "itself and its offspring" is written in the passage concerning consecrated offerings [where the night follows the day], it was necessary to expound it, as is taught in the Gemara:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:15:3.hebrew: מעשה בראשית - "ויהי ערב ויהי בקר" — ברישא ערב, והדר בקר:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:15:3.english: The act of Creation - "And there was evening and there was morning" — first evening, and afterward morning:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:16:1.hebrew: לפי שכל הענין - הפרשה הזאת סמוכה לקדשים, דכתיב "ירצה לקרבן אשה", וסמיך ליה "אותו ואת בנו":
Rashi on Chullin 83a:16:1.english: Because the entire section - This passage is adjacent to [the laws of] sacrifices, as it is written: "it shall be accepted for a sacrificial fire-offering" [Leviticus 22:27], and adjacent to it is [the prohibition of] "itself and its offspring" [Leviticus 22:28].

Rashi on Chullin 83a:16:2.hebrew: בקדשים לילה הולך אחר היום - דכתיב (ויקרא ז): "ביום קרבנו יאכל לא יניח ממנו עד בקר", אלמא לילה שלאחריו קרי "יום קרבנו" עד הבקר:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:16:2.english: With regard to sacrificial [animals], the night follows the day - as it is written (Leviticus 7[:15]): "On the day of his offering it shall be eaten; he shall not leave any of it until morning" — thus [the verse] calls the night that follows it "the day of his offering," until the morning:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:1:1.hebrew: בא הכתוב ליתן עשה - טעמא דבא הכתוב, הא לאו הכי לקי, אע"ג דהתראת ספק היא, דכל אימת דאתרו ביה, מצי אמר "אכתי ליליא הוא":
Rashi on Chullin 83a:1:1.english: The verse comes to provide a positive [commandment] - The reason [he is not flogged] is that the verse comes [to provide a positive commandment], implying that if not for this, he would be flogged — even though it is an uncertain forewarning, for whenever they forewarn him, he can say, "It is still night":

Rashi on Chullin 83a:2:1.english: This is not for that reason - He is not exempt [from lashes] for this reason:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:2:2.hebrew: שאין בו מעשה - ישב לו ולא אכל, ומאליו נעשה נותר:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:2:2.english: That does not involve an action - He sat [idly] and did not eat, and of its own accord it became notar [leftover sacrificial meat]:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:3:1.hebrew: משתי ירכות - של שתי בהמות, ומדנקט שתי בהמות שמע מינה בימינות קאמר, ות"ק דהכא כרבי יהודה ס"ל, דאין נוהג אלא באחת: ומהא פשטינן בפרק גיד הנשה (לקמן חולין דף צא.) דפשיטא ליה לר' יהודה דבימין:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:3:1.english: From two thighs - of two animals. And since [the baraita] specifies "two animals," infer from this that it is speaking of the right [thighs], and the Tanna Kamma here holds like Rabbi Yehuda, that [the prohibition of the sciatic nerve] applies only to one [thigh]. And from this [baraita] we resolve in Chapter Gid HaNasheh (below, Chullin 91a) that it is obvious to Rabbi Yehuda that [it applies] to the right [thigh]:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:5:1.hebrew: דלית ביה כזית - בקמא או בבתרא, אלא בחד מינייהו. ות"ק מחייב, דקסבר בריה הוא, ובריה [אין] צריכה שיעור, כדתנן במסכת מכות (דף יג.): אמר להם רבי שמעון: אי אתם מודים לי באוכל נמלה כל שהוא [שהוא] חייב? אמרו לו: מפני שהיא כברייתה. ואית דמפרשי דלית ביה כזית בחד מינייהו, אלא בתרוייהו; ואין נראה בעיני שיהו שתי התראות מצטרפות, דאי אכיל ליה לבתרא בתוך כדי אכילת פרס, היינו בבת אחת, ואי לאחר כדי אכילת פרס, תו לא מצטרפי:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:5:1.english: Where it does not have an olive-bulk - [That is, either] in the first [nerve] or in the second, [such that there is an olive-bulk] only in one of them. And the first Tanna [the Rabbis] holds him liable [for both], because he holds that [the sciatic nerve] is a complete entity (beryah), and a complete entity does not require a minimum measure, as we learned in a Mishnah in Tractate Makkot (13a): Rabbi Shimon said to them, "Do you not agree with me regarding one who eats an ant of any size, that he is liable?" They said to him, "[That is] because it is in its natural state [as a complete creature]." And there are those who explain that there is not an olive-bulk in [either] one of them [alone], only in both of them [combined]; but it does not seem right to me that two forewarnings should combine, for if he eats the second within the time span of eating a half-loaf (kedei achilat peras), that is [considered eating them] all at once, and if [he eats it] after the time span of eating a half-loaf, they no longer combine:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:5:2.hebrew: עד שיהא בו כזית - דקסבר לאו בריה חשיב, אלא כחתיכה מן הבהמה:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:5:2.english: Unless it has [a volume of] an olive-bulk - For he holds [that the sciatic nerve] is not considered a complete entity [beryah], but rather like a piece from the animal:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:6:1.hebrew: בארבעה פרקים בשנה - דרך ישראל לעשות סעודות, וסתם הלוקח בהמה אינו לוקח אלא לשוחטה מיד, לפיכך המוכר בהמה לחבירו, ומכר תחלה אמה או בתה בו ביום, צריך שיאמר לשני: דע לך שהיום מכרתי אמה לשחוט, או בתה מכרתי לשחוט, שמא כבר נשחטה:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:6:1.english: On four occasions during the year - [it is] the custom of Israel to make feasts, and ordinarily one who buys an animal only buys [it] to slaughter it immediately; therefore, one who sells an animal to his fellow, and had first sold its mother or its daughter on that same day, must say to the second [buyer]: "Know that today I sold its mother to slaughter," or "I sold its daughter to slaughter," lest it has already been slaughtered:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:6:2.hebrew: ביום טוב האחרון של חג - היו מרבין בשמחה, מפני שרגל לעצמו הוא וחביב עליהן:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:6:2.english: On the last festival day of the festival [of Sukkot] - they would increase [their] rejoicing, because it is a festival unto itself and is beloved to them.

Rashi on Chullin 83a:7:1.hebrew: שאין לו ריוח - הפסק בינתים, שמכר האם היום:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:7:1.english: That he has no interval - [meaning] a gap in between, [i.e.,] that he sold the mother today:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:7:2.english: But [if] he has an interval - [meaning] that he sold the first [animal] yesterday and the second today:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:7:3.hebrew: אין צריך להודיעו - שאני אומר, אתמול שחט הראשון:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:7:3.english: He does not need to inform him - For I say, the first [buyer] slaughtered [his animal] yesterday:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:7:4.hebrew: ומודה רבי יהודה כו' - אע"פ שלקח זה היום וזה למחר:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:7:4.english: And Rabbi Yehuda concedes, etc. - Even though this one bought today and that one [bought] tomorrow:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:8:1.hebrew: משחיטין הטבח בעל כרחו - כדמפרש ואזיל, שאם קבל דינר מלוקח ליתן לו בדינר בשר:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:8:1.english: One compels the butcher to slaughter against his will - as [the Mishnah] goes on to explain, that if he received a dinar from a buyer to give him a dinar's worth of meat:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:8:2.hebrew: אפילו שור שוה אלף זוז - שוחטו על כרחו, אף על פי שאין לוקחין לשאר, ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:8:2.english: Even [if] a bull [is] worth a thousand zuz - he [the butcher] slaughters it against his will, even though there are no buyers for the rest [of the animal], and in the Gemara [it] explains the reason:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:8:3.english: And the buyer has only one dinar in it - [meaning] that he gave a dinar to the butcher:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:8:4.english: It dies at [the expense of] the buyer - and he loses the dinar:

Rashi on Chullin 83a:8:5.hebrew: אינו כן - דבעינן משיכה, וכל זמן שלא משך, חוזר בו הטבח:
Rashi on Chullin 83a:8:5.english: It is not so - For we require pulling [to effect acquisition], and as long as [the buyer] has not pulled [it], the butcher may retract:

Tosafot on Chullin 83a:6:1.hebrew: וכדברי רבי יוסי הגלילי אף ערב יום הכפורים בגליל - תימה, דבריש כתובות (דף ה.) פריך: יום הכפורים שחל להיות בשני בשבת ידחה, גזירה שמא ישחוט בן עוף; ואמאי לא פריך משאר ימים טובים, דהוי לכ"ע? ואומר ר"ת, דבשאר ערב י"ט שוחטין בהמות, כדאמר הכא, אבל ערב יוה"כ לא היו אוכלין אלא בשר עוף ודגים, כדאמר בב"ר גבי ההוא דזבן נונא. והא דלא חשיב הכא ערב יו"ט ראשון של חג, אומר ר"ת משום דכולי עלמא טרידי בסוכה ולולב, ואין להן פנאי להרבות בשחיטה כל כך:
Tosafot on Chullin 83a:6:1.english: And according to the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, the eve of Yom Kippur in the Galilee as well - This is astonishing, for at the beginning of Ketubot (5a) [the Gemara] asks: Yom Kippur that falls on Monday should be postponed, [as] a decree lest one slaughter a young bird! Why does it not ask from other festivals, which apply according to everyone? And Rabbeinu Tam says that on the eve of other festivals they slaughter animals, as [the Mishnah] states here, whereas on the eve of Yom Kippur they would eat only the meat of fowl and fish, as it says in Bereishit Rabbah regarding that [man] who bought a fish. And as for [the fact] that [the Mishnah] does not count here the eve of the first festival day of Sukkot, Rabbeinu Tam says [it is] because everyone is preoccupied with the sukkah and the lulav, and they do not have time to slaughter so abundantly:

Tosafot on Chullin 83a:7:1.hebrew: ומודה רבי יהודה - תימה, למאן מודה? ד"אימתי" דרבי יהודה לפרש הוא, כדאמרינן בסנהדרין בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כה.):
Tosafot on Chullin 83a:7:1.english: And Rabbi Yehuda concedes - This is astonishing: to whom does he concede? For [the expression] "When" of Rabbi Yehuda is [meant] to explain [the Sages' ruling], as we say in Sanhedrin in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 25a):
